narrative: The model estimated a 52% chance that you will leave your job, meaning it sees your departure as slightly more likely than your staying. Because that risk is above the halfway mark, your promotion was denied. The most influential factor was whether you had other job opportunities. You reported none, and about 77% of employees predicted to stay also had none, so this factor pushed toward staying. The second most influential factor was your six to ten years in this organization, which also pushed toward staying and is common among employees predicted to stay. The third factor was your six to ten years of total experience, which pushed toward leaving. Although two of the top three signals were protective, many smaller factors combined to lift the estimated risk just above half. Going forward, the organization should discuss your career path, recognition, and promotion timeline with you. Since you have no alternative opportunities and moderate tenure, targeted development and clearer advancement prospects could reduce the perceived leaving risk.
